meta.name: Match lost and found items with OpenAI, SendGrid and Google Sheets

name: Match Lost and Found Items with OpenAI, SendGrid and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Lost & Found Item Matcher

This workflow logs lost and found item reports from airports, hotels, or transit desks, uses OpenAI to validate and normalize each freeform report into structured data, searches existing reports on file for the best possible match, and emails both parties via SendGrid once a confident match is found — with every case tracked in Google Sheets.

### Who's it for
- Airport lost & found desks handling dozens of reports a day
- Hotel concierge teams reconciling guest lost-item reports
- Transit authorities (rail, bus, rideshare) matching lost items to claims
- Any front desk that wants to stop manually cross-checking spreadsheets

### How it works
1. A desk agent or online form submits a POST request with report type (lost/found), item description, location, date, and contact info
2. OpenAI normalizes the freeform description into structured fields — category, color, brand, distinguishing features — and flags whether the report is valid/complete
3. Existing opposite-type reports (found reports for a lost item, or vice versa) are pulled from the Google Sheets log
4. A Python scoring engine compares the new report against every candidate on file, weighing category, color, brand, location, and date proximity
5. The best match is selected; if its confidence score clears the threshold, AI drafts a warm, clear match notification
6. SendGrid emails both the original reporter and the matched reporter with the match details and a claim reference
7. Every report — matched or still pending — is logged to Google Sheets for audit and future rematching
8. The webhook returns the full outcome (matched, pending, or invalid) as JSON

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add OpenAI credentials to both OpenAI Chat Model nodes
3. Add a SendGrid API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SENDGRID_API_KEY) and attach it to both Send Email nodes
4. Replace YOUR_VERIFIED_SENDER with a SendGrid-verified sender address
5. Add Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all three Sheets nodes
6. Activate the workflow and POST a test lost report, then a matching found report

### Requirements
- OpenAI API key (GPT-4.1-mini or above)
- SendGrid account with a verified sender identity
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials

### How to customize
- Adjust the match confidence threshold in JS - Select Best Match (default: 75/100)
- Adjust scoring weights in Python - Score Candidate Matches (default: category 40%, color 20%, brand 20%, location 10%, date 10%)
- Add photo-similarity scoring by extending the AI normalization step with an image URL field
- Swap SendGrid for another ESP by changing the HTTP request URL/body in the Send Email nodes
- Add SMS fallback (Twilio) alongside email for high-value item matches

### Google Sheets Column Layout
Set up your ReportsLog tab with these headers in row 1:
Report ID | Date | Timestamp | Report Type | Category | Color | Brand | Location | Date Lost/Found | Description | Contact Name | Contact Email | Matched Report ID | Match Score | Status

## 1. Trigger & Report Intake

Accepts new lost/found reports via webhook POST in real time, or runs a periodic sweep every 15 minutes (useful for retrying rematches against reports that arrived after an earlier unmatched report).

Required POST fields: reportType (lost/found), itemDescription, location, dateLostFound, contactName, contactEmail.

The Set node normalizes all fields and generates a unique requestId. This raw report is then handed to OpenAI for validation and structuring.

## 2. AI Normalization & Candidate Fetch

The AI - Normalize & Validate Report agent reads the freeform description and location text and extracts structured attributes: category, color, brand, distinguishing features, a cleaned description, and an isValid flag with any missing fields.

JS - Parse AI Normalization safely parses that structured output and merges it with the original report. Filter - Valid Report routes incomplete or unparseable reports to an error handler that immediately returns a clear error to the caller.

Valid reports move on to Fetch Existing Opposite Reports, which pulls every pending report of the opposite type (lost vs found) from the Google Sheets log so they can be compared against the new report.

## 3. Scoring & Match Selection

The Python scoring engine compares the new report against every candidate pulled from the sheet, computing a weighted composite score from category match, color match, brand match, location match, and how close the dates are.

JS - Select Best Match sorts all scored candidates and picks the top result, flagging isConfidentMatch when the score clears the threshold (default 75/100). Below that threshold, the report is logged as still pending rather than force-matched.

## 4. Notify & Log

If a confident match was found: AI - Generate Match Notification Message drafts a calm, clear email explaining the match and a claim reference number, without oversharing sensitive contact details. JS - Format Match Emails builds two SendGrid payloads — one for the original reporter, one for the matched reporter — and both are sent via SendGrid, each with continueOnFail so an email outage never blocks the webhook response.

If no confident match yet: the report is simply logged as Pending so future incoming reports can be matched against it.

Either way, the case is appended to the Google Sheets log, and the webhook returns the full outcome as JSON.
